angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 348,546 km at 29.80 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 33.5601 +/- 0.0141 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 29.80 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.501 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Gan et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 1815 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract): 348,546 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.502 +/- 0.015 solar masses from Gan et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 1815 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3643 +/- 142 K from Gan et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1815 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gan et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1815 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-1815.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.739, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1815 (pscomppars): spectral type M1, from Gan et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1815 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.12 dex, from Gan et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1815 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.38722, from Gan et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1815 (pscomppars): rotation period 47.8 d, from Gan et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..160G/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, L 181-1: projected rotation speed 1.65 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2022ApJS..259...35A)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
